title: Swing-fraction skewness fails to establish incremental Parkinson prediction across two public gait collections
abstract: We tested whether the third standardized moment of within-foot swing-time fraction adds information beyond demographics and conventional gait summaries. Source-only logistic models trained on31 gaitndd participants were frozen and applied to151 gaitpdb participants after excluding two known identical opposite-label recordings. External Brier score changed from 0.327821 to 0.335676; Swing-fraction skewness did not establish incremental cross-dataset Brier benefit: delta +0.007855, joint95% interval [-0.028931,+0.043978] in31 source and151 target participants. AUC decreased from 0.673281 to 0.654146. Broad uncertainty, small training size and exploratory dataset reuse preclude equivalence or absence-of-information claims.
